division.heading: Request for Particulars, Amendments to Pleadings and Close of Pleadings

operative_text.controlling:
3.67(1)  This rule applies to pleadings between the following:
(a) a plaintiff and a defendant;
(b) a plaintiff-by-counterclaim and a
defendant-by-counterclaim;
(c) a third party plaintiff and a third party defendant;
(d) a plaintiff and a third party defendant.
(2)  Pleadings close when
(a) a reply is filed and served by a plaintiff, plaintiff-by-
counterclaim or third party plaintiff, as the case may be,
or
(b) the time for filing and serving a reply expires,
whichever is earlier.
(3)  The close of pleadings against one party represents the close of
pleadings against all parties to that pleading.

BOOK_B.operative_text_raw: (1) This rule applies to pleadings between the following: (a) a plaintiff and a defendant; (b) a plaintiff-by-counterclaim and a defendant-by-counterclaim; (c) a third party plaintiff and a third party defendant; (d) a plaintiff and a third party defendant. (2) Pleadings close when (a) a reply is filed and served by a plaintiff, plaintiff-by-counterclaim or third party plaintiff, as the case may be, or (b) the time for filing and serving a reply expires, whichever is earlier. (3) The close of pleadings against one party represents the close of pleadings against all parties to that pleading.

BOOK_C.title: Close of pleadings

commentary.text: Close of pleadings is very important. It is the point when all of the issues in the action are framed. It is the starting point for the need for leave of the court or consent of all parties to amend pleadings pursuant to rule 3.62. Pleadings close when any one of the enumerated parties serves a reply, or the time for filing and serving a reply ( Hislop v. Murray, [2012] AWLD 4638, 219 ACWS (3d) 248 at para. 22 (Alta. Q.B. (Master)). days from receipt of the statement of defence) expires, whichever is earlier. Importantly, the close of pleadings against one party is the close of pleadings against all parties to that particular pleading.
